static_traits.name: Li Yi
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy or similar psychological problem experience
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and scenes specifically; negative attitude; willing to cooperate with counseling; able to identify one's negative thought patterns

basic_info.main_problem: I have always thought my name is very ordinary and boring, which makes me feel inferior and lacking uniqueness. These feelings about my name have existed since I can remember, affecting my self-esteem. The belief intensifies especially in Social situations or when introducing myself.
basic_info.core_demands: I just want to no longer feel inferior because of my name; I want to find ways to be more confident and unique.

core_beliefs: I am very ordinary, utterly unremarkable

special_situations.event: Introducing oneself to strangers in social settings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my name is ordinary, people will think I am ordinary too, not worth noticing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids or simplifies self-introductions, reduces contact with strangers
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am just an ordinary person in the crowd

special_situations.event: Hearing others call one's name in public
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When I feel I am ordinary, it proves I really am ordinary
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to ignore or distract to reduce discomfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This reminds me again that I am just an ordinary person in the crowd

special_situations.event: Asked for one's name when meeting for the first time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the name is not unique, I cannot leave a good impression
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding in-depth conversation, quickly ending self-introductions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My name is so boring, with no highlights at all

special_situations.event: When talking with friends, thinks about sharing his troubles about his name
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express this worry, others will find me childish or making a fuss
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not disclosing this trouble to friends, choosing silence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am being unreasonable, ridiculous

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and recognized as a unique and valuable person
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being ignored for being 'ordinary', evaluated as boring, thus losing self-worth
defense_goal: Protecting self-esteem by repressing related feelings, avoiding self-introductions and not sharing troubles, avoiding negative evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: An ordinary person not worth noticing
object_relations.object_representation: Picky people who judge oneself by one's name

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite a detailed description of emotions and experiences related to names
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Li Yi subconsciously believes others will see him as 'ordinary, not worth noticing', intensifying shame and avoidance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle, empathic and non-judgmental tone; inviting him to specify scenes and name emotions; using open-ended questions to help him gradually contact rather than avoid emotional experience.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes positive reframing or challenges the negative labels of 'ordinary/boring'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Li Yi believes change is unlikely ('this part of me is too long-standing'), thereby maintaining current cognitive stability
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Acknowledging his worries and doubts, using small gradual goals; applying joint evidence review and behavioral experiments, avoiding argumentative persuasion.

manifestations: Tightly binding 'whether the name is unique' with 'whether the self is meaningful/valuable'
In socializing and self-introductions, experiences the feeling of being 'just an ordinary person in the crowd'

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and harsh self-reproach, is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly concerned about how others view one's name and uniqueness
Repeatedly self-evaluates and worries before and after self-introductions

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not sharing name-related troubles with friends, choosing silence and bearing alone
Turning the impulse to expect others' understanding into self-repression

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Choosing to ignore or distract when hearing the name triggers discomfort
When self-introduction is required, tries to quickly skim past and avoid deep communication

exception_events.target_problem: When meeting new friends or needing to introduce himself, Li Yi usually feels inferior and anxious due to the belief 'I am very ordinary', tending to avoid or shorten interactions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At a gathering with close friends, Li Yi did not worry as usual about whether his name was ordinary, but communicated more comfortably, experiencing higher confidence and relaxation.
exception_events.reason: Different support and situation: friends already know him and the interaction is safe, reducing worry about external evaluation; the stable relationship atmosphere shifted his attention from 'the name's uniqueness' to genuine interaction.

positive_force: Has a stable friend support network in which to experience confidence and security
Willing to seek help and try to change (has sought counseling)
Able to identify and describe one's negative cognitive patterns
negative_force: Excessive reliance on external evaluation to affirm self-worth
Negative cognitive biases are marked (Mental Filtering, Overgeneralization, All-or-Nothing Thinking, Disqualifying the Positive, Mind Reading)
Rigidly binds the name to self-worth, forming a rigid negative label

target_behavior.behavior: Anxiety and avoidance when introducing oneself in Social situations, with significant negative self-evaluation
antecedent: Asked for one's name when meeting for the first time
Being called by name by others in public
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing 'ordinary name' into 'ordinary self, not unique', and predicting others will belittle him for it, triggering inferiority and Anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential negative evaluation and shame, briefly reducing Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, increased social stress, impaired interaction quality, further reinforcing the belief 'I am very ordinary'

target_behavior.behavior: Not sharing name-related troubles with friends, choosing silence
antecedent: Thinking about expressing this trouble when talking with friends
When talking about self-image or confidence
target_behavior.core_reason: Worried about being seen as childish or making a fuss, makes mind-reading inferences and avoids possible evaluation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of embarrassment and being negated, maintaining surface security
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty obtaining reality testing and emotional support, negative beliefs uncorrected and continuously solidified
